L87: Agent SDK
L88: # Quickstart
L89: 
L90: Get started with the Python or TypeScript Agent SDK to build AI agents that work autonomously
L91: 
L92: Copy page Copy page
L93: 
L94: Use the Agent SDK to build an AI agent that reads your code, finds bugs, and fixes them, all without manual intervention. What you’ll do:
L95: 
L96:   1. Set up a project with the Agent SDK
L97:   2. Create a file with some buggy code
L98:   3. Run an agent that finds and fixes the bugs automatically
L99: ##
L100: 
L101: cite41†​ L102: 
L103: Prerequisites
L104: 
L105:   * Node.js 18+ or Python 3.10+
L106:   * An Anthropic account. If you don’t have one, cite50†sign up here†platform.claude.com .
L107: ##
L108: 
L109: cite42†​ L110: 
L111: Setup
L112: 
L113: 1
L114: 
L115: Create a project folder
L116: 
L117: Create a new directory for this quickstart:
L118: 
L119:     `mkdir my-agent
L120:     cd my-agent
L121:     `
L122: 
L123: For your own projects, you can run the SDK from any folder; it will have access to files in that directory and its subdirectories by default.
L124: 
L125: 2
L126: 
L127: Install the SDK
L128: 
L129: Install the Agent SDK package for your language:
L130: 
L131:   * TypeScript (new project)
L132: 
L133:   * TypeScript (existing project)
L134: 
L135:   * Python (uv)
L136:   * Python (pip)
L137: 
L138:     `npm init -y
L139:     npm pkg set type=module
L140:     npm install @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk
L141:     npm install --save-dev tsx
L142:     `
L143: 
L144: Setting `"type": "module"` in `package.json` lets your agent script use top-level `await`, and cite51†tsx†tsx.hirok.io runs TypeScript files directly. npm prints `added N packages` when the install succeeds.
L145: 
L146:     `npm install @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk
L147:     npm install --save-dev tsx
L148:     `
L149: cite51†tsx†tsx.hirok.io runs TypeScript files directly. If your project uses CommonJS, name your agent script `agent.mts` instead of `agent.ts`. The `.mts` extension makes tsx treat the file as an ES module, so top-level `await` works without converting your whole project to ES modules. Use `agent.mts` in place of `agent.ts` in the create and run steps later in this quickstart.
L150: cite52†uv†docs.astral.sh is a fast Python package manager that handles virtual environments automatically:
L151: 
L152:     `uv init
L153:     uv add claude-agent-sdk
L154:     `
L155: 
L156: Create and activate a virtual environment, then install the package.On macOS or Linux:
L157: 
L158:     `python3 -m venv .venv
L159:     source .venv/bin/activate
L160:     pip install claude-agent-sdk
L161:     `
L162: 
L163: On Windows:
L164: 
L165:     `py -m venv .venv
L166:     .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
L167:     pip install claude-agent-sdk
L168:     `
L169: If PowerShell blocks `Activate.ps1` with an execution policy error, run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process RemoteSigned` first.
L170: 
L171: Both the TypeScript and Python SDKs bundle a native Claude Code binary, so most installs need no separate Claude Code install. Some installs have no bundled binary:
L172:   * If pip installs the Python SDK’s source distribution instead of a platform wheel, for example on ARM64 Windows, no binary is bundled. cite53†Install Claude Code natively . The Python SDK finds it on your `PATH`.
L173:   * The TypeScript SDK installs its binary through npm optional dependencies, so an install that skips them, for example `npm ci --omit=optional`, gets no binary even on a supported platform. Reinstall without skipping optional dependencies, or cite53†install Claude Code natively and set `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` to its path.
L174: 3
L175: 
L176: Set your API key
L177: 
L178: Get an API key from the cite50†Claude Console†platform.claude.com , then set it as an environment variable in the shell where you’ll run your agent:
L179: 
L180:   * macOS / Linux
L181: 
L182:   * Windows (PowerShell)
L183: 
L184:     `export REDACTED
L185:     `
L186: The SDK reads the key from the environment of the process that runs your agent; it doesn’t load `.env` files automatically. If you keep the key in a `.env` file, load it yourself, for example with the `dotenv` package, before calling the SDK.The SDK also supports authentication via third-party API providers:
L187:   * Amazon Bedrock: set `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1` environment variable and configure AWS credentials
L188:   * Claude Platform on AWS: set `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS=1` and `ANTHROPIC_AWS_WORKSPACE_ID`, then configure AWS credentials
L189:   * Google Cloud’s Agent Platform: set `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1` environment variable and configure Google Cloud credentials
L190:   * Microsoft Foundry: set `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1` environment variable and configure Azure credentials
L191: See the setup guides for cite54†Amazon Bedrock , cite55†Claude Platform on AWS , cite56†Google Cloud’s Agent Platform , or cite57†Microsoft Foundry for details.
L192: Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK. Please use the API key authentication methods described in this document instead.
L193: ##
L194: 
L195: cite43†​ L196: 
L197: Create a buggy file
L198: 
L199: This quickstart walks you through building an agent that can find and fix bugs in code. First, you need a file with some intentional bugs for the agent to fix. Create `utils.py` in the `my-agent` directory and paste the following code:
L200: 
L201:     `def calculate_average(numbers):
L202:         total = 0
L203:         for num in numbers:
L204:             total += num
L205:         return total / len(numbers)
L206: 
L207: 
L208:     def get_user_name(user):
L209:         return user["name"].upper()
L210:     `
L211: This code has two bugs:
L212: 
L213:   1. `calculate_average([])` crashes with division by zero
L214:   2. `get_user_name(None)` crashes with a TypeError
L215: ##
L216: 
L217: cite44†​ L218: 
L219: Build an agent that finds and fixes bugs
L220: 
L221: Create `agent.py` if you’re using the Python SDK, or `agent.ts` for TypeScript. Use `agent.mts` instead if your existing project uses CommonJS:
L222: 
L223: Python
L224: TypeScript
L225: 
L226:     `import asyncio
L227:     from claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions, AssistantMessage, ResultMessage
L228: 
L229: 
L230:     async def main():
L231:         # Agentic loop: streams messages as Claude works
L232:         async for message in query(
L233:             prompt="Review utils.py for bugs that would cause crashes. Fix any issues you find.",
L234:             options=ClaudeAgentOptions(
L235:                 allowed_tools=["Read", "Edit", "Glob"],  # Auto-approve these tools
L236:                 permission_mode="acceptEdits",  # Auto-approve file edits
L237:             ),
L238:         ):
L239:             # Print human-readable output
L240:             if isinstance(message, AssistantMessage):
L241:                 for block in message.content:
L242:                     if hasattr(block, "text"):
L243:                         print(block.text)  # Claude's reasoning
L244:                     elif hasattr(block, "name"):
L245:                         print(f"Tool: {block.name}")  # Tool being called
L246:             elif isinstance(message, ResultMessage):
L247:                 print(f"Done: {message.subtype}")  # Final result
L248: 
L249: 
L250:     asyncio.run(main())
L251:     `
L252: 
L253:     `import { query } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk";
L254: 
L255:     // Agentic loop: streams messages as Claude works
L256:     for await (const message of query({
L257:       prompt: "Review utils.py for bugs that would cause crashes. Fix any issues you find.",
L258:       options: {
L259:         allowedTools: ["Read", "Edit", "Glob"], // Auto-approve these tools
L260:         permissionMode: "acceptEdits" // Auto-approve file edits
L261:       }
L262:     })) {
L263:       // Print human-readable output
L264:       if (message.type === "assistant" && message.message?.content) {
L265:         for (const block of message.message.content) {
L266:           if ("text" in block) {
L267:             console.log(block.text); // Claude's reasoning
L268:           } else if ("name" in block) {
L269:             console.log(`Tool: ${block.name}`); // Tool being called
L270:           }
L271:         }
L272:       } else if (message.type === "result") {
L273:         console.log(`Done: ${message.subtype}`); // Final result
L274:       }
L275:     }
L276:     `
L277: This code has three main parts:
L278:   1. `query`: the main entry point that creates the agentic loop. It returns an async iterator, so you use `async for` to stream messages as Claude works. See the full API in the cite58†Python or cite59†TypeScript SDK reference.
L279:   2. `prompt`: what you want Claude to do. Claude figures out which tools to use based on the task.

The Agent SDK does not solve subscription OAuth for a web app.

There are three distinct things:

- OpenAI Agents SDK uses the Responses API with Platform credentials and usage-based API billing. A ChatGPT subscription does not authenticate it.
- OpenAI Codex SDK can reuse a user’s ChatGPT subscription, but it runs a local Codex process. Twyne could support this in its desktop app by launching `codex login`; it cannot provide the same capability from the hosted web app. [OpenAI Codex authentication](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth), [Codex SDK](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex-sdk)
- Anthropic Agent SDK explicitly does not permit third-party products to offer Claude.ai login or consume users’ Free/Pro/Max limits without prior approval. Anthropic requires API-key or supported cloud-provider authentication for that use case. [Anthropic Agent SDK overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview), [authentication policy](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance#authentication-and-credential-use)

So the viable product is:

- Twyne desktop: “Sign in with ChatGPT” through the local Codex SDK, consuming the user’s Codex subscription.
- Twyne web: Responses API through an OpenAI API key.
- Anthropic: API key by default; subscription sign-in only if Anthropic grants Twyne explicit partner approval.
- Keep provider credentials local and show the exact billing source in Settings.

Also, the `ant auth login` layer I added authenticates an Anthropic Console workspace—it does not turn a Claude Pro/Max subscription into Twyne inference. I should relabel or remove it rather than imply otherwise.
